# Abrams r1 at 128px: follow-up review

**Verdict:** The real 128px render is visually acceptable as a restrained first pass. At 128px it introduces no visible defects: no chalk lines, no wireframe look, no shimmering or aliasing artifacts, and no false joints. But at 128px the accents add almost no readability. The pass gives a small gain in a few views at 256px and close to nothing at 128px. **It is not a dramatic improvement from every angle, and that claim isn't supported.** I don't see an unresolved core-category defect in the static source that should block structured evaluation.

## What the 128px render shows (`recognition-128-r1.png`, tiles about 127px)

| View | Accent effect at 128px |
|---|---|
| **Front** | Best case. A dark mark at the mantlet can still be seen, but at this size you can't separate the mantlet-square accent from the gun-bore shadow and the diagonal antenna shadow. |
| **Top** | The rear grille and the two hatch cupolas read as blobs. The blow-off panel outlines and hatch-lid seams have mostly gone. |
| **Physical left/right** | The tank reads clearly as an M1-type tank. I can't make out the skirt panel seams. The skirt reads as one band with wheel shadows below it. |
| **Front and rear ¾** | It reads as a tank. I can't tell it apart from what r33 would look like at this size. |

This matches what I estimated before: at 128px one pixel covers about 7 cm, and the accents are 1.8–2.6 cm wide, so they mix into the paint colour. At 128px, separation comes from geometry, cast shadow and the existing material contrast, not from the new lines.

**Presentation note (not a model defect):** At 128px the tile labels take up a large share of each tile, and "rear three-quarter" is cut off at the tile edge. Before any named human review, use a labeled copy with the labels placed outside the tiles.

## Corrections accepted

- **Skirts:** If the source export shows seven separate panel solids, the seam accents follow real per-panel boundaries. I withdraw my "design choice, not boundary" comment.
- **Shoe011:** It is inherited as the `LeftTrack`/`RightTrack` datum objects. That resolves the gap.
- **Object count:** 270 = 260 meshes + 10 retained non-mesh objects. That matches 246 + 14.
- **Native isolation:** The receipt is 8.4 MB, so I only read the header. It shows profile `native-rigid-isolation-v1`, `complete: true`, `unsupportedFeatures: []`, and per-object SHA-256 hashes for objects and materials. I did not check each of the 26 probe results one by one.
- **Scope:** Accepted. Animation and game-distance z-fighting are separate qualifications. I'm dropping them as static blockers, because I found no visible evidence of z-fighting in any provided render.

## Core categories (static source, after the 128px render)

| Category | Score | Strongest remaining objection |
|---|---|---|
| identity-recognition | **3** | It reads as an M1 at 128px in every view, but that recognition already existed in r33. The accents add nothing at 128px. |
| silhouette | **3** | Unchanged from r33. At 128px the thin antennas are the only outline feature that stands out. |
| mechanical-coherence | **3** | At 256px the hatch, blow-off, mantlet and skirt separation reads better. The turret-to-hull and driver-hatch separation still relies on shadow. That's an improvement left undone, not a defect. |
| production-integrity | **3** | The static source checks out: source geometry retained, accents owned by the right parts, isolation complete, and no visible artifacts. Scored without the separate animation and engine work. |

## Answers to your questions

- **Acceptable as a restrained first pass?** Yes. It is restrained, it follows real part boundaries, and it is visually clean at both 128px and 256px.
- **Does it fully meet the request to separate similar-coloured parts at distance?** Only in part. You can see the effect at about 256px in the top, front and physical-right views. At 128px it has essentially no effect. If the user means distance as 128px or smaller, a later pass would need wider or higher-contrast accents. The other route is separation by value or material on the parts themselves.
- **Unresolved core-category blocker for static source?** None that I found.
- **Merits human review?** Yes, once the structured evaluation and adversarial review are complete. When you present it, describe the gain as modest and near the pixel limit, mainly at 256px, not a dramatic improvement from every angle.
- **Status:** `technicalValidation` passed for the static source. `visualRecommendation` is pending the structured evaluator, with no category objection from me. `humanApproval` is none.

I made no edits.
